def: A DNA sequence that reads the same 5' to 3' on both strands. Many restriction enzyme recognition sites are palindromic.
DNA sequences that read the same 5' to 3' on both strands. Many restriction enzyme recognition sites are palindromic.
Inflammation of all three layers of the heart (endocardium, myocardium and pericardium). It is a major feature of acute rheumatic fever.
Affecting the entire lobule or acinus. Panlobular emphysema destroys the whole acinus and is typical of alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, mainly in lower lobes.
Describes skin lesions that are raised (papules and plaques) with scale. Psoriasis, lichen planus, pityriasis rosea and secondary syphilis are papulosquamous diseases.
Relating to cells in the layer just above the basal layer of the epithelium. Parabasal cells in a Pap smear are small immature cells seen with atrophy or after menopause.
Beside the colon. The paracolic gutters are peritoneal spaces running along the ascending and descending colon that let fluid or pus spread in the abdomen.
Abnormal sensation such as tingling, pins and needles or burning without an outside stimulus, caused by nerve irritation or damage.
Brand name of a hormone-free copper intrauterine device. Copper creates an inflammatory environment toxic to sperm and eggs, and it also works as emergency contraception.
Muscle stiffness triggered by cold or repeated activity that worsens with exercise, unlike usual myotonia. Paramyotonia congenita is caused by a sodium channel mutation.
Describes speech errors in which wrong sounds or words are substituted, as in Wernicke aphasia. Phonemic errors replace sounds; semantic errors replace words.
A chemical in hair dyes and black henna tattoos that is a common cause of allergic contact dermatitis (a type IV hypersensitivity reaction).
A hepatitis C protease inhibitor (NS3/4A) used in combination regimens with ritonavir and other antivirals.
An exaggerated skin reaction, with a pustule or ulcer, at the site of a minor injury such as a needle prick. It is characteristic of Behcet disease.
A potassium binder taken by mouth that exchanges calcium for potassium in the gut, lowering serum potassium in hyperkalemia.
Containing few cells. A paucicellular bone marrow or tumor has sparse cellularity.
Clear transmission of spoken or whispered words through the chest wall on auscultation, heard over consolidated lung such as in pneumonia.
A polyethylene glycol-linked bovine adenosine deaminase given as enzyme replacement for adenosine deaminase-deficient severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID).
The zone of brain tissue around a stroke core that is poorly perfused but still alive and potentially salvageable if blood flow is restored quickly.
Surrounding the cerebral aqueduct in the midbrain. The periaqueductal gray is a key region for pain modulation, receiving input that triggers descending pain suppression.
The dense connective tissue sheath covering cartilage that supplies it with nutrients and new cells. Articular cartilage lacks it.
The connective tissue sheath surrounding a bundle (fascicle) of muscle fibers, between the endomysium and epimysium.
New bone formation under the periosteum, the membrane covering bone. It occurs in hypertrophic osteoarthropathy and chronic venous disease.
Older name for the fibularis muscles of the lateral leg, which evert the foot. The peroneal (fibular) nerve supplies them.
An outer membrane protein of Bordetella pertussis that helps it adhere to respiratory cells. It is a component of acellular pertussis vaccines.
Recording penile erections, typically during sleep, to tell psychological from organic causes of erectile dysfunction (nocturnal penile tumescence testing).
A drug that gives the body an alternative route to excrete nitrogen waste. It is used for urea cycle disorders and works by binding glutamine.
The compound whose N-methylation by phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase in the adrenal medulla turns norepinephrine into epinephrine. Cortisol induces this enzyme.
Describes sand flies (subfamily Phlebotominae), which transmit Leishmania, sandfly fever and Bartonella bacilliformis.
Drugs that improve venous tone and reduce vein leakage, such as flavonoids (diosmin), used for chronic venous disease and hemorrhoids.
Severe inflammation or swelling from deep venous thrombosis. Phlegmasia cerulea dolens is a massive, painful, blue swollen limb from extensive clotting that threatens limb survival.
The glycolysis enzyme (phosphoglucose isomerase) that converts glucose 6-phosphate to fructose 6-phosphate. Its deficiency causes hemolytic anemia.
Sunburn of the cornea from ultraviolet light, such as from welding arcs (arc eye), tanning or snow glare. It causes severe pain, tearing and light sensitivity hours after exposure.
Connecting the diaphragm and colon. The phrenicocolic ligament supports the spleen and anchors the splenic flexure of the colon.
Toad-skin: rough, bumpy, horny follicular plugs on the skin, classically from vitamin A deficiency, though sometimes from deficiencies of essential fatty acids or B vitamins.
A family of small, nonenveloped, positive-sense single-stranded RNA viruses, including poliovirus, coxsackievirus, echovirus, rhinovirus and hepatitis A virus.
Relating to the hair follicle and its attached sebaceous gland. Acne occurs when pilosebaceous units are blocked and inflamed.
A topical calcineurin inhibitor used for atopic dermatitis. It blocks T-cell activation without steroid skin thinning.
A short-acting beta-2 agonist inhaler that relaxes bronchial smooth muscle, used for asthma.
An antifibrotic drug that slows decline in lung function in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis by reducing fibroblast activity and TGF-beta signaling.
A statin that lowers cholesterol by inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase.
A histamine H3 receptor antagonist and inverse agonist used to treat daytime sleepiness and cataplexy in narcolepsy.
Pointing the foot downward at the ankle, away from the shin, as when standing on tiptoe.
Resembling plasma cells, with eccentric nuclei and basophilic cytoplasm. Plasmacytoid dendritic cells produce large amounts of type I interferon in viral infection.
A thin sheet of muscle across the front of the neck, supplied by the facial nerve (cranial nerve VII), that tenses the neck skin and pulls down the jaw corner.
Relating to the platysma, the thin neck muscle supplied by the facial nerve. Platysmal bands are vertical cords visible in the aging neck.
Describes a single gene or factor that affects multiple, seemingly unrelated traits or actions. Marfan syndrome is pleiotropic.
Variation in the size and shape of cells and nuclei within a tissue, a hallmark of malignancy and anaplasia.
Between the pleural and peritoneal cavities. The pleuroperitoneal membranes help form the diaphragm, and failure of closure causes congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
Disorders of a nerve plexus, such as the brachial or lumbosacral plexus, causing weakness, numbness and pain in its distribution.
A disorder of a nerve plexus such as the brachial or lumbosacral plexus, causing weakness, numbness and pain in its distribution.
Describes the pneumotaxic center, a pontine group of neurons that limits inspiration and raises breathing rate.
Having a body temperature that varies with the environment rather than being regulated. In people, it can appear after spinal cord injury or hypothalamic damage.
Describes a single mRNA that codes for several proteins. Prokaryotes, such as the lac operon, make polycistronic mRNA, while eukaryotic mRNA is usually monocistronic.
Another name for fibrocystin, the protein encoded by PKHD1. Mutations cause autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease.
Attachment of several glutamate residues to a molecule, which traps it inside cells. Folate and methotrexate are polyglutamated.
Polyribosylribitol phosphate (PRP) is the capsule polysaccharide of Haemophilus influenzae type b, the antigen in the Hib vaccine.
The lateral cerebellar hemispheres (also called cerebrocerebellum), which receive cortical input through the pons and help plan and time voluntary movement.
A small muscle at the back of the knee that unlocks the knee by rotating the femur laterally on the tibia at the start of flexion.
